---
title: "Compositions: stack and concat"
---



A VRT places each source file into a slab of the destination array. xvrt
supports two ways of laying sources along one dimension.

| | `concat` | `stack` |
|---|---|---|
| the dimension | already exists in each file | is new, one position per file |
| each file contributes | its own length along it (1 or more) | exactly one position |
| typical input | daily or monthly NetCDF with a `time` dim | 2D files, one per date or level |

## concat: files that already have the dimension

::: {#3d42a437 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import xarray as xr
from xvrt import write_mdim_vrt
from _fixtures import daily_netcdf

paths = daily_netcdf(n=3)
ds = xr.open_mfdataset(paths, combine="nested", concat_dim="time")
out = write_mdim_vrt(ds, paths, paths[0].parent / "concat.vrt",
                     composition="concat", concat_dim="time")
```
:::


xvrt needs to know how many steps each file contributes. It works it out in
this order: the `sizes=` argument; a `size` in dict-form sources; the
Dataset's dask chunks when there is one chunk per file (the
`open_mfdataset` default); an even split when the total divides by the number
of files (with a warning, because it is a guess); and finally opening each
file to read its length. Passing `sizes=` is the explicit route:

::: {#45275022 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
out = write_mdim_vrt(ds, paths, paths[0].parent / "concat.vrt",
                     composition="concat", concat_dim="time", sizes=[1, 1, 1])
```
:::


The concat coordinate must be strictly monotonic, and by default it is
written inline (or as start and step when regular). `coord_mode={"time":
"source"}` instead reads it from every file, slab by slab, which only makes
sense when all files store it in the same units.

## stack: one file per position of a new dimension

Here the files are 2D and the Dataset gets a new dimension when they are
combined:

::: {#46e28238 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from _fixtures import slices_2d

paths = slices_2d(n=3)
parts = [xr.open_dataset(p) for p in paths]
ds = xr.concat(parts, dim="level").assign_coords(level=[0.0, 10.0, 20.0])
out = write_mdim_vrt(ds, paths, paths[0].parent / "stack.vrt",
                     composition="stack", concat_dim="level")
print("\n".join(l for l in out.read_text().splitlines() if "Source" in l or "View" in l)[:900])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
      <Source>
        <SourceFilename relativeToVRT="1">temp_level0.nc</SourceFilename>
        <SourceArray>/temp</SourceArray>
        <SourceView>[newaxis,...]</SourceView>
        <SourceSlab offset="0,0,0" count="1,3,4" step="1,1,1" />
      </Source>
      <Source>
        <SourceFilename relativeToVRT="1">temp_level1.nc</SourceFilename>
        <SourceArray>/temp</SourceArray>
        <SourceView>[newaxis,...]</SourceView>
        <SourceSlab offset="0,0,0" count="1,3,4" step="1,1,1" />
      </Source>
      <Source>
        <SourceFilename relativeToVRT="1">temp_level2.nc</SourceFilename>
        <SourceArray>/temp</SourceArray>
        <SourceView>[newaxis,...]</SourceView>
        <SourceSlab offset="0,0,0" count="1,3,4" step="1,1,1" />
      </Source>
```
:::
:::


A 2D source cannot fill a 3D slab directly (GDAL refuses sources whose rank
differs from the destination), so each source gets a view that adds the
length-1 axis: `<SourceView>[newaxis,...]</SourceView>`. Files that already
carry a length-1 dimension of that name (one time step per file) need no
view; xvrt checks the first file's metadata to tell the two apart, or you can
say so with `"has_dim": True` in dict-form sources.

## Gaps: placing sources by index

In a stack, a dict-form source can carry an explicit `"index"`, its position
along the stack dimension. Positions without a source read as nodata, which
is how a collection with missing days is described:

::: {#a92cbda2 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from osgeo import gdal
gdal.UseExceptions()

srcs = [{"path": str(paths[0]), "index": 0}, {"path": str(paths[2]), "index": 2}]
out = write_mdim_vrt(ds, srcs, paths[0].parent / "gaps.vrt",
                     composition="stack", concat_dim="level")
a = gdal.OpenEx(str(out), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER).GetRootGroup().OpenMDArray("temp")
a.ReadAsArray()[:, 0, 0]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5}
```
array([10., nan, 12.], dtype=float32)
```
:::
:::


Either every source has an index or none does.

## Source forms

Sources are a list of paths or URLs (`http(s)://` becomes `/vsicurl/`,
`s3://` becomes `/vsis3/`), or dicts:

```python
{"path": "file.nc", "size": 31}          # concat: steps in this file
{"path": "file.nc", "array": "/sst"}     # source array name, if it differs
{"path": "day.tif", "band": 1}           # raster band source (GeoTIFF/COG)
{"path": "day.tif", "index": 42}         # stack position
```

Local paths below the VRT's folder are written relative to it.
